sections.text: The wise call him a sage, for whatever he undertakes is free from the motive of desire, and his deeds are purified by the fire of Wisdom.
Having surrendered all claim to the results of his actions, always contented and independent, in reality he does nothing, even though he is apparently acting.
Expecting nothing, his mind and personality controlled, without greed, doing bodily actions only; though he acts, yet he remains untainted.

What is my purpose and destiny? So we had been discussing chapter four, Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga -- Yoga of renouncing actions in knowledge. Not physically renouncing actions, but renouncing attachment to them through knowledge. How to not identify with your actions.
So far we have seen that Bhagavan said Ajaha -- I am Ajaha, Im unborn. Therefore he is also Amara. Therefore he is deathless.
One who has no birth cannot have any death. So because he is Ajaha, he is also Amara. And not only that, but he says, I am a Karmaha, I am actionless, I am birthless, I am deathless, also actionless.
So at the macro level he says, Im not participating in anything that you consider is happening. It is only happening because of my presence. But I am not actively participating in it because I dont have any desire to get anything out of it.
There is no desire for Karma Phala of these actions, therefore I am not involved in it. Even the action is taking place because of his presence. But because he is not involved in it, with any desire to gain anything out of it, he is actionless.
Same thing applies at a micro level to our self, which we constantly call it I that I am, I am. But then everything we say after that I am, that I is not involved in it. I am working, I am speaking.
So all the words which we attach to I and am that existence, I is not involved in it. So Bhagwan says, who is involved in that action? Then the one who consider that to be the actor is involved in it. That I, when I say I am eating, thats a physical act, so the body is involved.
Then when I say I like what I eat, my mind is involved. And then my intellect says, this is pretty nutritious, so Im going to get some benefit out of it. My intellect is involved.
Whatever gets involved, thats the one which is bound by its results. So once the I is not involved as the actor and therefore remains Actionless. That which gets involved will be bound by the actions and therefore has to receive the results.
So my body is involved in my physical act. So more exercise I do or less exercise I do, more I eat or less I eat will show up in my body. When I go to my doctor, he figures out that you may not have been doing this or you may not be watching your diet.
Because my lab results tell him exactly. All that tells him what I had been doing. So the body is bound by its own actions.
Whatever the grudges and complexes I carry, they will show up in my mental attitude. So the mind is bound by what mind does. Then what I learn or not learn will show up at my intellectual level.
So this body, mind and intellect are bound by these actions. Till I get attached to that body, mind and intellect, I am not involved and actionless. But as soon as I identify with this body, mind and intellect, I become the doer.
And that doer is, aham, the ego. Once the ego is formed, that ego becomes the enjoyer and sufferer of these actions. So now who are we trying to really liberate right now? Not the body, not the mind, not the intellect.
Ego is the sufferer and enjoyer. That ego is trying very hard to redeem itself. Achieving a state where there is no unhappiness, there is no sorrow and there is no death.
So that ego is trying very hard to achieve that by actions. Because it can only attach itself to the body, mind and intellect. And therefore it says, let me achieve this.
I can achieve security by accomplishing things and acquiring things. Or I can achieve deathlessness by finding all the latest cures about or anti aging drugs, whatever that is. And its failing miserably.
No matter how hard I try, I think Im not aging. But other people say, Rajan, you look little old now. My nephews and nieces.
Kaka, now you look a little tired. And what do you mean? We are trying very hard to achieve what we are trying to achieve through the means available to us right now. But we are not getting there.
So Bhagavan said, the only one way to achieve is you disassociate yourself from actions. But actions cannot stop. So say that you have to achieve that knowledge where you start seeing inaction in actions.
Actions are being performed. The only entity which is inactive in this is my self. My self is not taking any part; my consciousness, just because it is there, makes all three function -- the body, mind and intellect.
A supervisor really doesnt do anything. On a factory floor, the supervisor is not operating machines, but his presence makes all the work go on. If hes not there, work will be all over the place.
I give my real life example a lot of times. I used to work in India in an architects firm, and my boss used to come to the United States every two years or so to renew his green card. During those four to six weeks he was here, we would have a complete vacation.
We all go to work every morning just as when he was there. We try very hard to work for about half an hour. And then somebody will say, You know, Rajan, did you know this? And he will start a topic and then everybody get involved.
We have about six, seven people in the same room. That topic will go on till lunchtime. Then we realize, oh God, we havent done anything.
Well, lets have lunch. And then after that we can work something. And that will go on till about four weeks.
And when we realize that one week my boss is going to come back, we start suddenly putting something on a paper which looks like we had done some work. In the end, there was no real work done when he was not there. And as soon as he comes, everything goes back to normal.
We are working, just as the supervisors presence makes all the workers work. But the supervisor really doesnt do the work himself. He doesnt sit down and start doing what he was supposed to do.
His presence make it work. But he is not participating in your activities the same way the self is not participating, but the very presence of the self, the consciousness make people work. But because right now my identification is with the workers, all the drawbacks and the quality of the workers become my qualities.
But if I identify with that self who is actionless, then Ill see myself as actionless too. Karmani Akarma Yahya Pashet -- one who sees inaction. Action only takes place when my ego gets involved. When I was in Zambia, it was so difficult to get a drivers license because the test was about 20 times more difficult than what you go through here.
And without a drivers license you cant do anything. So you are so keen on getting a drivers license, you work so hard, and your mind and intellect are both involved in driving so intensely. Last week I told somebody, You know, Im trying very hard to remember everybodys name. And she said, dont try too hard.
That was the problem -- I was putting too much mental effort into it. So when Im trying too hard to drive the car, its very difficult. But now when I drive, I dont consider that as a real action requiring effort because my mind and intellect are not intensely involved while Im driving -- it has become automatic.
So Bhagavan said, when you do that, you reach a level where all your actions you see just as what you see, youre driving, you are literally removed. You have your mind and intellect are free to think about other things. Karmaniya, Karmaiya, Pashet, Karmani, Chakarma Yaha.
Not only that, but even though it seems inaction, but action is taking place. By not acting also you are doing something which is affecting you. Sabuddhiman, Manusheshu.
Out of all these people who consider themselves intellectuals, such a person is a wise one. Sabuddhima and Manish Yeshu, he is a Buddhiman. He is a true intelligent person who figured out that actions are taking place at the level of body, mind and intelligence, not at my self level.
Sahayuktaha, Such a person is Yogi. He is connected Yogi, one who is connected with the self. As we have seen at a macro level, the supreme self, the God is everywhere, is omniscient, omnipotent and omnipresent.
At micro level, myself is omnipresent, omniscient, omnipotent. In my this body, mind and intellect. When I see that is myself, Im connected with that self.
So Sai Yuktah, Krishna Karmakrit and such a person knows how to act. In this world we are all acting but at a very lesser capacity. I think they say you are only using the 1/10 of the capacity of your brain.
Our brain has so much capacity, but we are only using it at a very micro level. Bhagwan said, if you then think about how capable you are when you connect to your higher self, then when you act, your actions will be perfect. Krishna, Karma, Krita, Such a person know how to perform real actions.
It actually says how to become efficient in life by connecting with your higher self. And then the next few verses actually give the prescription for how to connect to that higher self. So now we have learned what the issue is.
The issue is that I consider myself to be a mortal being who has birth, who is acting in this world and suffering. Bhagavan said, no, no, youre birthless, youre deathless and you have all the capacity to work in this world -- you just have a wrong identification. So yes, we hear this word Samaram in our vernacular language.
When there is some event taking place -- Samaram. For whom are all events taking place in his life? Kama Sankalpa Varjita -- there should be Kama Sankalpa Varjita. Kama means desire.
Sankalpa is translated here as planning; I would say determination. What are we determining? I want to do this and I want to get out of this. So first I have a desire.
I want to make million dollar, then make a plan. How am I going to make a million dollar? That plan is based on what Ill get a million dollar out of it. So all my actions are first starts with the desire, then I have a plan to achieve that particular results out of that action.
And therefore Im bound to fail. Because first of all I have not figured out whether what I desire is really appropriate for my capability. And secondly, whether the plan Im putting together action Im putting together or capable of achieving it.
Because only thing available to me as I said in this world is knowledge of my actions. I do not have knowledge about how the world is going to react to these actions but Im still determining what the results would be. Therefore there are more unknowns than knowns in my actions.
There are more chances of failure than success. So: do not have any desire and do not have any plan to get something out of it. Kama Sankalpa Varjita. Gnana Agni Dagda Karmanam -- I am acting in this world, but all my actions are burnt with the fire of knowledge.
The knowledge that this body, mind and intellect are limited in their capabilities. But the self which is involved in these actions is only a Sakshi Chaitanya -- a witness -- and he is not affected by any of these actions.

These verses describe the qualities of a true sage (pandita): one whose every undertaking is free from desire and selfish planning (kama-sankalpa-varjita), whose actions are burned in the fire of knowledge (jnanagni-dagdha-karmanam). Such a person, though apparently acting, does nothing at all (naiva kinchit karoti sah), because they have surrendered attachment to results and remain ever content and independent (nitya-tripto nirasrayah). The culmination is verse 21: expecting nothing, with controlled mind, abandoning all possessiveness, performing only bodily actions, one incurs no sin (kilbisham).
The teaching here addresses the fundamental error: we identify with the doer and therefore become bound by results. The ego is the sufferer and enjoyer, not the Self. When we act from desire (kama) and planning for specific outcomes (sankalpa), we plant seeds that must bear fruit. But when actions arise spontaneously from our nature without personal agenda, they leave no karmic residue. It is like the difference between a new employee desperate to impress versus a master craftsman who simply does excellent work because that is who they are.
For todays practice, before each significant action, pause and ask: What desire is driving this? What outcome am I planning and attached to? Practice tyaktva karma-phalasangam - releasing attachment to results before you begin. Notice how this changes the quality of your engagement. When you finish an action, practice letting it go like a post-it note that leaves no mark. The sage acts only at the bodily level (shariram kevalam karma) - meaning the deeper Self is uninvolved. Can you act today with your body and skills fully engaged while your inner witness remains detached, content, and free?
